clue.text: Copulates like a rabbit — is jumpy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a buck is a male rabbit, and to buck is to mate as one does
second meaning: a startled horse leaps and kicks in just this way

explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes it look like one description of a nervous rabbit; it is two separate senses of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The male rabbit's name doubles as its verb for mating, and a horse that leaps with arched back does the same word.

clue.text: Vulgar Othello, for instance, can

parts.note: broad humour is coarse or vulgar
Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: A sneer at a crude Othello, perhaps a bad production, ending in a dangling 'can'.
explanation.walkthrough: BROADMOOR is the high-security psychiatric hospital in Berkshire, England, where dangerous offenders are locked up; 'can' is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for a jail, and this secure institution holds criminals behind locked doors, so it serves as one.

clue.text: Interrupts flipping TUC initially something rotten!

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters of the union's initials run backwards

parts.note: taken as written: the Trades Union Congress

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of something
food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: An exasperated 'flipping TUC' cutting in on a rant, with the union branded rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' is a mild British oath in the surface but the turnaround signal in the wordplay, making CUT; 'initially' picks one opening letter. The TUC is Britain's federation of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone off is to stop them mid-sentence, which is what interrupting a speaker means.

clue.text: Have intercourse with speed to reach climax

definitions.note: intercourse in its old sense of conversation and dealings with others

parts.note: s is the symbol for speed in the school physics formula s = d/t
to peak is to reach the highest point

explanation.surface: Advice on hurrying sex to its climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intercourse' leads to sex, but the definition uses its older sense of conversation; 'with' and 'to' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Social intercourse means talking and dealing with people, so to communicate in words is to have intercourse.

clue.text: Calumnist proffers rear to Mike Tyson type

parts.note: the back is the rear of something
the boxer Mike Tyson bit off part of Evander Holyfield's ear in a 1997 bout

explanation.surface: A slanderer offering his behind to a heavyweight who bites, a picture of comic peril.
explanation.walkthrough: Calumnist is a coinage on 'columnist': one who spreads calumny, a fair jab in a satirical magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks spitefully of people behind their backs is a slanderer, one who spreads calumny.

clue.text: Throw up on getting into an embrace, resulting in telling-off!

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means the word is written from the bottom upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw high
locking is clasping or getting into a lock, as wrestlers or lovers do

explanation.surface: Someone vomits mid-cuddle and gets roundly scolded for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means written bottom to top, giving BOL; 'on' then sits the embrace beneath it. The answer is British slang for a severe scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe reprimand is called this in British slang, an earthy word for a dressing-down.

clue.text: Frightens BSE victims

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cow someone is to intimidate them
second meaning: cattle were the animals struck by mad cow disease

explanation.walkthrough: BSE, bovine spongiform encephalopathy, was the 'mad cow disease' scare in 1990s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb meaning intimidates and the plural of the farm animal hit by the disease are spelt the same.

clue.text: One who gets briefs off Britt's timeless rear

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or awry, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
less time: a T, the abbreviation for time, is dropped

parts.note: the name Britt with its possessive s, read as the letters BRITTS
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone removes the underwear of Britt, presumably the actress Britt Ekland, from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefs' looks like underwear, but a brief is a case handed to a lawyer. 'timeless' drops a T from BRITTS to leave BRITS, and 'off' rearranges BRITS with REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In England a solicitor instructs a courtroom advocate by sending a brief, so receiving them is that advocate's job.

clue.text: He scored, giving prostitute one in back

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: back means the little word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who 'scored' by paying a prostitute, then the rest of the encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests sexual conquest; here it means wrote music. 'back' gives NI. Giuseppe Tartini was an 18th-century Italian violinist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to write music for instruments, and the Italian violinist wrote many sonatas, so he is a man who scored.

clue.text: Lover-boy Cyclops in short jumper

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a roo is the short form of kangaroo, a jumping animal
Cyclops is the setter's pen name, so the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter himself, as a ladies' man, in a skimpy sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is a sweater in Britain, which the surface leans on; the jumper here is the kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young lover gave his name to any amorous young man, a familiar term for a ladies' man.

clue.text: How Clinton spoke to certain senators with Monica present?

definitions.text: How Clinton spoke to certain senators with Monica present?

parts.words: How Clinton spoke to certain senators with Monica present?
parts.note: Lewinsky testified that Clinton took telephone calls while she performed oral sex on him, so the phrase for 'on the phone' doubles as a joke

explanation.walkthrough: Blower is British slang for the telephone; the phrase means speaking by phone, while 'blower' also points at Monica Lewinsky's role.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means talking by telephone, which is how the President spoke to the senators.

clue.text: Drive home a sexually aggressive type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to force a point or a nail home by striking hard
second meaning: the male sheep, used of a lustful man

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests giving a pushy date a lift; the two halves are separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to force in hard, and the male sheep gives its name to a lustful, forceful man.

clue.text: Turn it to enter shag area arse-over-elbow

indicators.note: British slang for head over heels, tumbling, so the whole string is turned to read backwards

parts.note: shag and bonk are both British slang for having sex
a rood is an old unit of land area, a quarter of an acre

explanation.surface: A crude instruction to tumble into a place for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arse-over-elbow', slang for head over heels, turns BONK plus ROOD end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle on a door is the thing you twist to get into a room, which the definition describes cryptically.

clue.text: Old politician needs one fleece for sexual appetite!

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal, a member of the party that merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988
I is the Roman numeral for one
to do someone is slang for swindling or fleecing them

explanation.surface: An elderly politician needing a woolly fleece to boost his flagging desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like the wool garment but here means to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The psychological term names sex drive, the desire that the definition calls an appetite.

clue.text: Stroke Brenda as a sweetener

parts.note: a backhand is a stroke in tennis
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, who is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Caressing the Queen to sweeten her up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' looks like a caress, but it is a racket shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is a bribe, and a payment slipped secretly is a bribe passed under the table.

clue.text: In bad taste, Clinton's vice, but just what the circling vultures want?

definitions.text: just what the circling vultures want

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad and tastes it
Al Gore was vice president under Bill Clinton

explanation.surface: A complaint that Clinton's sexual vice is tasteless, with the press as circling vultures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice' suggests a moral failing, but it is the vice president.
explanation.definitionFit: Vultures feed on carcasses and discarded entrails, the waste parts of a slaughtered animal.

clue.text: Endure dyke right to the very end

parts.note: to last is to endure
a dyke is a ditch or drainage channel

explanation.surface: A provocation built on the slang sense of 'dyke' for a lesbian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dyke' plays on its slang sense; in the parse it is a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is one made at the final moment, holding out to the end.

clue.text: Tinky's other half involved with rats and villains alike

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are jumbled together

parts.note: Tinky Winky is the purple Teletubby, so the second half of his name follows Tinky
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Teletubby outed by an American preacher in 1999, now mixed up with rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' jumbles WINKY and RATS. The KRAY TWINS, Ronnie and Reggie, were identical twin gangsters who ran London's East End in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical twin brothers who were both notorious gangsters are villains who look alike.

clue.text: Don't expect fancy strokes with such characters

definitions.text: Don't expect fancy strokes with such characters

parts.words: Don't expect fancy strokes with such characters
parts.note: characters here are printed letters, and the fancy strokes are the little finishing lines at the ends of their stems

explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' and 'strokes' suggest people and sporting or amorous flair; they are letters and pen strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface without serifs, the decorative cross-strokes, is named with the French for 'without'.

clue.text: Decline hits familiar rogue dealer, we hear, one who won't follow orders

parts.note: to decline is to refuse

indicators.note: we hear means the next piece is spelt by its sound, not its usual spelling

parts.note: Nick Leeson, whose rogue trading broke Barings Bank in 1995, known familiarly by his first name

explanation.surface: A fall in markets hitting the trader who wrecked Barings Bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a market slump; it is the verb. 'we hear' turns NICK into the same-sounding NIK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet term for someone refused permission to emigrate now names anyone who refuses to obey.

clue.text: Local cinema bound to enter attack

indicators.note: to enter means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a fit is an attack of illness or temper
to bound is to leap

explanation.surface: Someone bound for the neighbourhood picture house to stage an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'heading for', but it is a jump, and 'to enter' sends it inside the attack. A fleapit is a shabby old cinema, British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang name for a run-down neighbourhood picture house supposes it is infested with insects.

clue.text: Cook a bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... Cook, Labour's Foreign Secretary at the time
second meaning: the red-breasted garden bird

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a kitchen instruction, but Cook is a surname and the answer his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The politician's given name is also the familiar red-breasted songbird.

clue.text: Bare tit wobbled cap that!

indicators.note: something that wobbled has been shaken about, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dare: a woman's exposed breast wobbled, and nobody can top that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbled' shakes up the letters of BARE TIT; 'cap that' suggests 'beat that', but the cap is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: This square, ridged hat is worn by Roman Catholic clergy, so it is a kind of cap.

clue.text: Avid to take on non-union issues, the union leader's view of fat cats

definitions.text: the union leader's view of fat cats

parts.note: avid means greedy
issue means offspring, and children born outside a marriage union were called bastards

explanation.surface: A trade unionist's outburst at greedy executives taking on non-union labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' is read two ways: a trade union in the surface, a marriage in the wordplay. Fat cats are overpaid bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade unionist would naturally curse overpaid company bosses in exactly these blunt terms.

clue.text: Nerd about right as description of Prince Philip?

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a geek is a nerd

explanation.surface: Calling the Queen's husband a nerd who goes on about being right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps GEEK around R. Prince Philip was born a prince of Greece and Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Born into the Greek royal family on Corfu, the Duke of Edinburgh could be called by that nationality.

clue.text: See 22
Right sweat loosening and dropping one's pants

indicators.note: loosening means the letters are shaken free into a new order
dropping means a letter is let fall from the word

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: Someone in a proper sweat, loosening and then dropping their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' lets the A fall from SWEAT to leave SWET, and 'loosening' rearranges R and SWET. Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pants means trousers in American English, and trews are tartan trousers.

clue.text: Potty character, name of Tony

parts.note: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men of 1950s children's television, so Ben is a pot character

explanation.surface: A dotty eccentric whose name is Tony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' means crazy in British English, a dig at Tony Benn, the left-wing Labour politician; the wordplay reads it as flowerpot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour veteran's first name was Tony, so the surname is what the forename points to.

clue.text: The Spectator has the ability to see things that are apparently not there!

definitions.text: the ability to see things that are apparently not there

indicators.note: has means the letters are held inside the words that follow, run across their join

parts.note: the run of letters sits across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A dig from Private Eye at its rival The Spectator for seeing things that are not there.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrasensory perception is the supposed power to perceive things beyond the normal senses.

clue.text: Fashion leader Tony's first split linked with Cyclops!

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter of Tony's
to rend is to split or tear
Cyclops is the pen name of the crossword's setter

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's first party split, laid at the setter's door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes T from 'Tony's'; 'split' looks like a party rupture but is a verb meaning tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who starts a new style that others copy leads fashion.

clue.text: Cook's place next to Brenda? Lord!

parts.note: a cook works in a kitchen
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, who is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The cook's quarters beside the Queen, with an oath at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord!' reads as an exclamation; it is the title. Lord Kitchener was the British field marshal of the 'Your Country Needs You' poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Field Marshal Herbert Kitchener was made an earl, so this soldier was a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Cane employees

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a walking stick or rod
second meaning: the people who work for an organisation

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a call to beat the workers; it is two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a long stick and the body of people employed by an organisation.
